claims.text: The damaged component is prone to hot cracking during traditional fusion-welding repair because of its microstructural characteristics.
Laser-based cold spraying can repair the damaged high-value component effectively.
Laser-based cold spraying can repair the component without inducing hot cracking.
The repair can enable continued component service under aggressive operating conditions.
Laser-based cold spraying produces metallurgical bonding between the deposited material and the substrate.
Laser-based cold spraying avoids the high-temperature metallurgical reactions associated with fusion welding.
Avoiding fusion-welding-associated high-temperature reactions reduces the risk of hot cracking.
Laser-based cold-spray repair will provide greater resistance to hot cracking than traditional fusion-welding repair.
Laser-based cold-spray repair will extend component lifespan relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
The proposed repair is applicable at operating temperatures up to 500 degrees Celsius.
The proposed repair is applicable at stresses up to 500 MPa.
Repair effectiveness may depend on material composition, component microstructure, and cold-spray process parameters.
